painting-same-place.caption:
I moved to a different country once. It is in the same place as the one I left. After a few years, I couldn’t understand the language I once spoke. Or else, the old words had opposite meanings in the new country. Initially, it was like a never ending holiday. No one was required to swear oaths. They just lived with each other, expecting nothing.

I found good work to do. I met a woman I love. My daughter knows nothing of the old country or the rituals that once defined my hours. We like to blow bubbles and chase them until they pop, laughing and not worrying about catching them, because, what would you do with a bubble if you caught it?

Hard times fell on my new home. There was never the right amount of anything. Men from the old country attacked, saying partisans were poisoning the river that divides the land. I don’t know if that is true, but I don’t know why anyone would poison the river. We all eat the same fish, after all.

The hard times were harder in the old country. I went there for a funeral. People approached me speaking gibberish, squeezing my shoulders and coyly brandishing weapons. I thought about getting weapons of my own, but realized it was useless. Later, It was revealed that ruling councils in both countries had formed a cartel. There was no poison in the river after all, just not enough fish. I suppose they swam to a place where people are less hungry.
